manifest.method: Relation views are harvested from the retained matcher output — every edge is an attachment, candidate, twin cross-reference or segment gate that build_current_pages already emitted. No pair is re-matched, re-scored or certified here, so these views cannot disagree with the dashboard. Shells reuse the build_road_groups key (funding zone + PAP + region + road title base, or work + municipality + province), so Groupings and Relations describe the same clusters. Competing nodes are rows with more than one candidate edge: the matcher left them open on purpose.

edge_kinds.chainage: Committed attachment — same road base, overlapping spans.
edge_kinds.scope_amendment: Committed attachment — scope change, delta booked.
edge_kinds.segment_scope: Attached for review only — spans share no overlap, delta NOT booked.
edge_kinds.fuzzy: Open possibility — title-similarity suggestion, consumes nothing.
edge_kinds.ambiguous: Open possibility — duplicate key, no automatic pairing.

state_definitions.committed_attached: Matcher paired this row and booked the amount delta. Identity stays provisional — no pair is manually certified — but the money moved.
state_definitions.review_attached: Paired for scope review only: measured station spans share no overlap, so these are different segments of one road. The amount delta is deliberately withheld from adjustment totals.
state_definitions.open_candidate: Unpaired, with one or more visible possibilities (title-similarity or duplicate-key suggestions). Nothing was consumed or committed.
state_definitions.duplicate_key: Unpaired inside a repeated exact key. No automatic pairing is possible without a human tie-break; amount alone must not decide it.
state_definitions.twin_cross_referenced: Unpaired, but an identical normalized title + region + zone + equal amount row sits unmatched on the other side under a different program section. Cross-referenced, never auto-paired.
state_definitions.unmatched_insertion: House row with no NEP counterpart and no suggestion. An insertion candidate — not a certified insertion.
state_definitions.unmatched_deletion: NEP row with no House counterpart and no suggestion. A deletion candidate — not a certified removal or cancellation.

states_note: One explicit state per row, assigned by rank so record order cannot change the answer: committed attachment outranks review-only attachment, which outranks duplicate-key and twin cross-references, which outrank open possibilities, which outrank a bare unmatched claim. This is a thin overlay keyed by the same row ids the dashboard already loads — join on id rather than expecting a second copy of each row. "rows" maps every row to [state_index, side_index]; "detail" adds the shell, matcher status, edge references and twin pointer for rows in shells that have a finding, competition, a twin or a measured span. States describe what the matcher did and what it withheld — none of them certify identity, and a state of committed_attached still means provisional, not proven.

finding_definitions.competing_candidates: One row carries two or more candidate edges. The matcher committed to at most one; the rest stay visible rather than being discarded.
finding_definitions.committed_with_rivals: The matcher committed a pair while other candidates for the same row remained plausible. The clearest case where the relation view and the dashboard legitimately disagree — read both.
finding_definitions.shell_amount_gap: Shell totals differ across sides and no attached pair explains the gap. Could be a split, a re-scope, or rows that belong elsewhere.
finding_definitions.zero_overlap_attached: Measured spans share no overlap. Attached for scope review; the amount delta is withheld from adjustment totals.
finding_definitions.cross_pap_twin: Identical row under different program sections on both sides, both left unmatched. Transfer or duplicate printing — unproven either way.
finding_definitions.unsupplied_shell: One side of a shell is fully paired while the other still holds rows: split / insertion candidates, or dropped / re-titled items.
